current.text: He is a locked-in starter for Atlanta. He is projected to start next to McCollum, Alexander-Walker, Johnson and Okongwu, with each starter playing 30-plus minutes.

Lu Dort is the main threat to his minutes. Experts still expect him to keep his starting spot. If Dort starts, it would likely be in place of CJ McCollum, and Dort and Daniels will mostly be staggered for spacing.
Atlanta has no true point guard. McCollum, Alexander-Walker, Johnson and Daniels share the ball handling.
Last season his steals fell by a third to about 2 per game and he shot about 18% from three. He shot over 30% from three over the last six weeks of the season.

Experts expect a bounce-back. His steals should rise toward 2.3 to 3 per game and his three-point shooting should improve, which would help his points, FG% and threes. They see little downside, because both numbers can hardly get worse.
His rebounding rose under a changed scheme after the Trae Young trade. He ranked about 40th after that trade. When he plays next to Daniels and Johnson, Okongwu is spaced away from the rim.
Experts rank him above his market ADP of about 60. Calls range from the 40s to around pick 52, which is round four or five.
In auctions he should go for 20 USD or more. Getting him at 17 USD is tremendous value. His Yahoo projected price of 17 USD is far above his average Yahoo cost of about 5 USD.
Atlanta's playoff schedule is 4-4-3 games in weeks 19 to 21. The team has 14 back-to-backs, but resting players is not a concern, and the team did not shut players down last season.
Atlanta is projected to win about 46 games and finish between fourth and eighth in the East.

durable.text: He is an elite steals player and a league outlier in steals. His steal totals vary from year to year.
He is an All-Defense player with excellent defensive metrics.
He grew up as a point guard and handles the ball. He can give 5 to 6 assists, so he is not only a steals player. At times he plays almost a big man role on offense.
He is a poor shooter and a poor scorer. His FT% and threes are weak for his position.
Take him when you need steals.
He is worth much more in category leagues than in points leagues.

note: He is a steals anchor who also adds assists, rebounds and solid FG% from a guard-forward spot. He fits punt FT% and punt 3PM builds. Yahoo values him at 17 USD and ESPN at 19 USD, but average costs are only 4.4 and 9.7 USD. Experts say he is worth 20 USD or more, so a price in the high teens or low 20s is a good buy, well below the 28 USD our league paid last season. Early in the season, check that his steals are back above 2.3 per game, that his three-point shooting stays above 30%, and that Lu Dort is not cutting into his minutes.
